heading: Κεφ. δʹ. — CHAP. IV.
paragraphs:
P. 10, 1.87.—“for taking stretches out the hands, but
for giving draws them in”] Graphic description of taking and
giving.

P. 10, 1.88.—“by thy hands thou shalt give a ransom for
they sins”] Beneficence is better than sacrifice. See Prov. xvii.6,
“By mercy and truth iniquity is purged.”

P. 10, 1.98—“thy slave”] As in the New Testament, so
here, the relation of master and slave is not denounced, but
regulated.
